newFinding.summary: Assessment id=5 is persisted with contentVersion=1, not 6.

writingContract.enforcementMeaning: ENFORCED_AS_APPROVED_GRADING_GUIDANCE. The approved rubric WRT_RUBRIC_V3 normalisationIntent.wordCountHandling states length below the minimum is reflected in task_achievement, only below two thirds of the minimum, and that a complete response slightly under the minimum is not capped. Rejecting a 59-word answer would contradict approved content, so the range is not a submission gate. The server computes the word count, stores it, and passes wordMin, wordMax, belowMinimum, belowTwoThirdsMinimum and aboveMaximum to the grader.
writingContract.wordCountConvention: value.trim() ? value.trim().split(/\s+/u).length : 0 - identical to the learner page's countWritingWords
writingContract.hardTextLimits: 2 to 2000 characters, unchanged; text is trimmed, never truncated
writingContract.persistence: DiagnosticWritingResponse, one row per (attempt, task), created once when the attempt completes; a replayed completion queues nothing
writingContract.runIdentity: gradingAttempts is the run number; claim and final write are conditional on (id, status, run)

gradingContract.rubricSelection: each task's rubricId; the worker refuses a missing rubric or one whose skill differs from the task (RUBRIC_MISSING / RUBRIC_SKILL_MISMATCH)
gradingContract.outputValidation: validateRubricGrade implements the approved aiGradingRequirements: every criterion present, integer within 0-4, no unknown criterion, non-empty feedback, malformed JSON rejected, and submissionRef must equal this submission (feedback referencing a different submission). Invalid output is retried once, then GRADING_FAILED.
gradingContract.taskScore: mean criterion score as a percentage of the 0-4 range, stored unrounded; skill aggregation and rounding stay with the scorer phase
gradingContract.graderSeam: DIAGNOSTIC_RUBRIC_GRADER token; returns RAW output and never validates itself

implementations.mock: MockDiagnosticRubricGrader - tests, DIAGNOSTIC_GRADER_MODE=mock, or MOCK_AZURE_SPEECH / NODE_ENV=test. Says nothing about grading quality.
implementations.modelWriting: rubric-structured JSON prompt through AiService.chat. NOT run against the real provider in C2.
implementations.modelSpeaking: REFUSES with SPEAKING_RUBRIC_GRADER_NOT_CONFIGURED. The rubric needs what the learner said; the only speech call in the codebase is scripted pronunciation against a reference text, which does not measure this construct. Fail-closed leaves the task GRADING_FAILED and retryable rather than storing a meaningless score.

gradingContract.runningAppNote: The development environment has no mock flag set, so in the running app Writing would use the unverified model prompt and Speaking would fail closed. No learner can reach V2 productive tasks today: id=5 is a DRAFT and the ACTIVE legacy form has none.

speaking: (none|QUEUED|GRADING|GRADED|GRADING_FAILED|SKIPPED) -> QUEUED on confirm, only while the attempt is IN_PROGRESS; replaces the recording and makes older jobs stale
QUEUED -> GRADING by the job owning this audioKey (conditional)
GRADING -> GRADED | GRADING_FAILED (conditional on audioKey + GRADING)
GRADING_FAILED -> QUEUED by retry: owner only, audio present, conditional; also after completion
QUEUED|GRADING -> GRADING_FAILED when BullMQ reports the job failed or stalled, only for the same audioKey
any -> SKIPPED while IN_PROGRESS; a queued job then goes stale
writing: (none) -> QUEUED once per task when the attempt completes, run 1
QUEUED -> GRADING by the job owning this run (conditional)
GRADING -> GRADED | GRADING_FAILED (conditional on run + GRADING)
GRADING_FAILED -> QUEUED by retry: owner only, run incremented, conditional
QUEUED|GRADING -> GRADING_FAILED on BullMQ failure or stall, only for the same run
stateMachine.results: speakingScore is computed from GRADED rows only and is null otherwise; Writing score is null unless GRADED; productivePending is true only for QUEUED/GRADING; GRADING_FAILED is reported as such, never as 0

isolatedE2E.honestCorrection: An earlier assertion expected the first task-2 recording never to be graded. It was graded - the worker finished before the re-recording arrived - which is legitimate: stale protection prevents an old job overwriting a newer recording, not an old recording being graded first. The assertion was corrected to what can be claimed; the late-stale-job case is asserted deterministically in the unit spec.
